items.content_html:
Summary

Add a behavioral "anti-feature" for contextmenu event listeners' currently-spec'd behavior of light dismissing popovers.

Test results and supporting details

This behavior is standard and a consequence of the current specification. It's not a desirable behavior, but a new desired behavior is not yet specified.

When the spec'd behavior changes, we can flip this behavioral subfeature to be deprecated. It'll eventually fall out of BCD, when all implementers drop the current behavior.

Related issues

  • Towards #30848
  • whatwg/html#10905
items.title: `contextmenu` event: add behavioral subfeature for popover light dismiss

Summary

Samsung Browser 31 is out. Update the browser release list, and manually update api.SharedWorker as it only partially uses mirror.

Test results and supporting details

Release notes (or at least dates) are available for the Windows version on their website (https://developer.samsung.com/browser/release-note/windows-release-note.html), but not for the Android version.

The release date is based on the earliest APK uploaded to APKMirror (https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/samsung-electronics-co-ltd/samsung-internet-for-android/samsung-browser-31-0-0-64-release/). Based on those APKs, the 30 and 31 series overlapped for about a month, but it appears that some users of the release channel received version 31 on 2026-09-23.

Samsung Browser 31 appears to use Chromium 148, based on https://chromiumchecker.com/ and manual inspection of collector results.

Related issues

None

items.content_html:
The https://collector.openwebdocs.org/ project (v10.21.2) found new features shipping in Chromium 159 beta which was released yesterday. Currently, the collector covers about 90% of BCD, so the following list might not be exhaustive. Also, if a feature is in Canary/behind flags, it is not considered here. If a feature is missing, one reason can be that the IDL is not yet in a specification or in webref.

Chrome 159 stable releases on December 8, 2026. This PR needs to be merged before/with the BCD release on December 3, 2026.

With this PR, BCD will consider the following features as shipping in Chromium 159:

items.content_html:
FF161 enables support for ClipboardItem custom formats (types prefixed with web ) by default on desktop and Android in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2053725

This updates api.ClipboardItem.type_web from preview to 161, and adds notes for the Firefox-specific read restrictions (the spec doesn't restrict reads by origin):

  • Custom formats can only be read if the clipboard contains same-origin content. Firefox treats data from other applications as cross-origin. https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2086505
  • Extensions with clipboardRead can read custom formats from any origin. https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2087427

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46463
items.title: FF161 ClipboardItem web custom formats enabled by default

items.content_html:
FF161 adds support for the setParameterOptions argument of RTCRtpSender.setParameters(), and its encodingOptions property (an array of objects with a keyFrame property), in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2057265

This adds api.RTCRtpSender.setParameters.setParameterOptions_encodingOptions_parameter. keyFrame is the only member of each encodingOptions item, so it doesn't get its own subfeature.

  • Chrome: 122. Added in chromium/chromium@b53076683b (refs/heads/main@{#1249577}), and https://chromestatus.com/feature/5161082937409536 says 122.
  • Safari: false. WebKit's RTCRtpSender.idl still declares only setParameters(RTCRtpSendParameters parameters).

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46464
items.title: FF161 RTCRtpSender.setParameters() setParameterOptions.encodingOptions

Summary

Adds the password_option subfeature under api.CredentialsContainer.create to reflect that passing a password option is not supported in Safari or Firefox.

Test results and supporting details

  • Ran npm run format, npm run lint, and the repository unit test suite locally with all checks passing.
  • Safari unsupported status: https://webkit.org/b/252908
  • Firefox unsupported status: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1156047
  • Note: Chrome 60 is inferred from CredentialsContainer.create() (Chrome 60) and PasswordCredential (Chrome 51) support rather than tested on a live Chrome 60 binary.

Related issues

Fixes #7941
items.title: Add password_option subfeature to api.CredentialsContainer.create

items.content_html:
Summary

Chrome 157 and 159 removes the Protected Audience API surface.

Test results and supporting details

This Chromium change removes the various navigator properties: https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/commit/7270d1697cac1d56b7f2cea82346076db5d43743.

Some APIs remain, mainly the ProtectedAudience interface itself. I can't confirm its removal just yet (it seems to be in either 159 or 160 but I get inconsistent testing results right now). This Chromium change says 159, but it's not removed in Browser Stack's Chrome 159, but it is removed in my local Canary 160. It might be that Browser Stack has an older build, so I decided to let this be inconclusive for now. This is conclusively removed now.

Related issues

  • https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/commit/7270d1697cac1d56b7f2cea82346076db5d43743
  • https://issues.chromium.org/issues/460501344
items.title: Protected Audience APIs: Chrome 157 removes most but not all
